title: Add post-provision smoke canary for Dedicated pools
author: Gabe Wilson
description:
Context: As part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint, we want a workload-realistic validation step after a GPU node (or pool expansion) is marked provisioned but before we declare it Ready for inference workloads. The existing post-provision checks cover driver parity + NCCL smoke + kubelet join, but we were still missing a fast end-to-end “serving path” signal (runtime boot, model load, tokenization, request/streaming, basic latency sanity). This PR adds a lightweight post-provision smoke/perf canary for Dedicated pools. It runs as a short-lived Job in the target cluster/pool, executes a small fixed prompt set against the local inference endpoint (or local runtime shim in dev), and emits a single structured result that the provisioning pipeline can treat as a gate.

What this does: (1) Adds a new canary mode: post-provision/dedicated_smoke. (2) Provides a Kubernetes Job template + runner that can be invoked by the provisioning orchestrator (via Helm values + CLI flags). (3) Implements a minimal inference check: warm-up request, then N requests (streaming optional) with token-count normalization and a bounded timeout. (4) Records result artifacts (JSON) and emits metrics: pass/fail, latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and failure reason category. (5) Adds guardrails for metric cardinality (no per-node labels; only pool_id, region, gpu_type, image_channel, canary_type). (6) Documents how to run locally and how the provisioning gate should consume results.

Key behaviors/constraints: The canary is designed to complete within ~3 minutes in the common case and never exceed 8 minutes (hard deadline) to avoid ballooning time-to-ready. Failures are categorized to be actionable (MODEL_LOAD, RUNTIME_BOOT, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, HTTP_5XX, AUTHZ, OUTPUT_INVALID, PERF_REGRESSION). The perf thresholds are intentionally loose for initial rollout; we only fail hard on catastrophic perf (tokens/sec below floor) or timeouts, and we emit a “warn-only” flag for borderline cases so SRE can tune without paging.

Rollout plan: This is gated behind a feature flag in the provisioning system (to be wired in control plane) and defaults to disabled. Initial enablement targeted at us-east / A100 Dedicated pools only (staged rollout).

Testing: Unit tests for result classification + JSON schema; integration test in kind using a stubbed inference endpoint; helm template tests; CI includes a smoke run of the runner with a mocked endpoint.

Follow-ups: (a) Wire result upload pointer into fleet-readiness-service validation artifacts (tracked in ENG-4822/PR in redwood repo). (b) Tune perf thresholds per GPU type once we have baseline data. (c) Add a small “embedding-only” canary variant for pools that don’t serve chat.

Risk: Low/medium. Primary risk is false negatives due to transient cold-start/model pull delays; mitigated via warm-up, bounded retries, and explicit classification. Also added conservative timeouts and backoff to avoid hanging provisioning.

illustrative_snippet: Example output artifact (written to /artifacts/result.json and optionally uploaded by caller): {"canary_type":"post-provision/dedicated_smoke","status":"PASS","pool_id":"ded-pool-123","region":"us-east-1","gpu_type":"A100-80GB","image_channel":"candidate","latency_ms_p50":412,"latency_ms_p95":901,"tokens_per_sec":128.4,"requests":8,"streaming":true,"failure_category":"","error":"","started_at":"2025-10-13T21:04:12Z","finished_at":"2025-10-13T21:06:01Z"}
review_conversation:
Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet): Can we guarantee this won’t add >10m to time-to-ready in failure modes (e.g. model pull stalls)? Also want failure categories to map directly to runbook steps.

Gabe Wilson (Author): Added hard deadline (8m) via context + Job activeDeadlineSeconds and explicit step timeouts. Also split MODEL_LOAD vs REQUEST_TIMEOUT vs HTTP_5XX so the runbook can point to image/model cache vs serving vs networking.

Aisha Bello (SRE): Metrics look good, but please remove pod/node identifiers from labels. We got burned recently with per-node tags. Also histogram buckets should be fixed and not per-config.

Gabe Wilson: Done. Labels now limited to pool_id/region/gpu_type/image_channel/canary_type and pool_id is sanitized (hash prefix) when enabled in shared environments. Buckets are static.

Sergio Costa (Obs): Can we emit a single gauge for “gate pass” and a counter by failure category? Easier alerting.

Gabe Wilson: Added counter perf_canary_runs_total{status, failure_category, ...} and gauge perf_canary_last_success_timestamp_seconds{...}. Latency remains histogram.

Ethan Park (Platform): How will provisioning orchestrator consume this? We need a stable CLI contract.

Gabe Wilson: Added --output-json and exit codes: 0 pass, 10 warn-only, 20 fail. Docs include expected invocation. Orchestrator can treat 10 as non-blocking initially.

Keiko Yamamoto (Autoscaling/Guardrails): Perf threshold floors should be extremely conservative for rollout. Suggest warn-only for perf regression and fail only on timeouts/errors.

Gabe Wilson: Adjusted: perf floor fail is only if tokens/sec < 25 (catastrophic), otherwise warn-only and continue. Timeout/error remains fail.

Aisha Bello: Please add a note about paging: we should ticket on failure rate initially, not page.

Gabe Wilson: Added note in docs; alerting rules live in observability-pack PR, but included recommended thresholds in doc.

Approvals: Vanessa Ortiz approved after deadline + categories changes. Aisha Bello approved after label changes. Sergio Costa approved after metric additions. Ethan Park approved after CLI contract notes.
ci_checks: CI summary (GitHub Actions): build (pass), unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), helm-template (pass), integration-kind (flaky then pass). Rerun: integration-kind failed once due to kind image pull timeout; rerun passed. Final status: green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Post-merge note: enablement remains off by default; staged rollout will be handled in provisioning feature flag (separate PR in control plane).
release_notes: Internal: Adds optional post-provision smoke/perf canary Job for Dedicated pools to gate readiness on a minimal end-to-end inference signal. Emits pass/fail + latency/tokens/sec metrics and structured artifacts for triage.
